featIpDesc: Point it at a host you already run. You get reachable ports, service versions, and matching CVEs sorted by severity. We scan from the internet side only — no login to your box, no agent required for this.
featDomainDesc: DNS records, TLS certificate and expiry, security headers, and detected stack in one snapshot. Good for catching a forgotten subdomain or an expiring cert. It is posture, not business-logic testing.
featMobileDesc: Upload the APK, AAB, or IPA you ship to guests or staff. We flag risky permissions, exported components, and secrets baked into the binary before the build reaches a store.
featAttachDesc: Put a target on a schedule and diff every run against the previous one, so a new open port shows up as a change and not as a surprise. One nmap on a Friday is a memory; a schedule is a control.
featWorkspaceDesc: Your NOC, your sysadmin, and the property contact read the same scan trail instead of forwarding PDFs. Roles and invites per org; credits stay on each login, not in one shared pot.
featAssetsDesc: Register IPs, domains, and apps under the names your team already says out loud, so a ticket reads "front-desk PMS" and not just an address. Each plan has a hard cap, so the list stays real.
featGuardDesc: One wazuh-agent per VM reports what is installed and running, and raises critical alerts. Inventory plus alarm on the box. It is deliberately thin — not a full SIEM console with dashboards to babysit.
featUptimeDesc: Probe a URL or TCP port from outside and record when it stops answering. Reachability only: it does not read CVEs, and it is not an SLA guarantee for your rack or your upstream.
featCreditsDesc: Scans draw from a credit balance on your account, so a heavy audit month costs more than a quiet one and nothing is metered behind your back. Pricing is not published on this page.

heroHeadline: Find internet-facing exposure, schedule it, then alarm on the box.
heroProduct: Security attach for colo, VPS, and hospitality stacks
heroSub: You are already paying for the rack, the VPS, and the property uplink. Sinexis attaches security to that: scheduled outside-in scans of your IPs, domains, and mobile builds, plus one thin agent on the VM for inventory and critical alerts. Periodic scan is not 24/7 SIEM. Host Protect reads disk through a helper on the machine and reports nothing when it finds nothing. One wazuh-agent per host. Not a human pentest.
authSubtitle: Sinexis — security attach for colo, VPS, and hospitality stacks
notFoundBody: That URL is not a Sinexis page. Head back home, or sign in to reach your workspace, scans, and Guard hosts.
stepScanDesc: Start with one IP, domain, or mobile build you are responsible for. The scan runs from the internet side and lands as an HTML report you can hand to a client or an auditor.
stepAttachDesc: Set the interval — weekly, monthly, whatever your change rate is. Each run is compared to the last, so you review the delta instead of re-reading the whole report.
stepWorkspaceDesc: Bring the team into the same org. Assets get real names, history stays in one place, and the person on shift tonight sees what the last scan found.
stepGuardDesc: Install one wazuh-agent on the VM. It reports installed packages and running services, then raises critical alerts. That closes the loop: Scan → Attach → Workspace → Guard.
siemNote: SIEM log search and Cases (incident tickets stored in our Postgres, not a Wazuh plugin) sit behind an ops flag and are not sold as a live feature here. Host WAF protection runs in your own nginx on your server — never on the Sinexis edge.
faqAuthQ: Do I need permission to scan?
faqAuthA: Yes. Scan only hosts, domains, and apps you own or are explicitly authorized to test in writing. If you manage a property or a client rack, get that authorization before the first run. Unauthorized scanning is not allowed.
faqPentestA: No. This is automated outside-in scanning on a schedule. It finds exposed services, weak TLS, missing headers, and known CVEs. It does not test business logic, chained abuse, or your booking flow. If a contract or audit requires a manual pentest, keep it — use this to stay clean between engagements.
faqDataA: Findings and reports stay in your workspace, visible to the members you invite. See the privacy policy for retention detail. Do not upload credentials or secrets you are not allowed to store off your own systems.
faqGuardQ: Guard vs SIEM vs Host Protect?
faqGuardA: Guard is the thin agent view: machine inventory plus critical alerts, no log-hunting UI. SIEM is log search plus Cases, which are incident tickets in our own Postgres, and it is off by default. Host Protect is a helper on the VM that reads web directories for on-box malware; if the helper is not installed or a path is unreachable, we say so and return no hits. We do not invent malware to fill a screen.
faqAgentA: No. One wazuh-agent per machine, enrolled once to your org. Host Protect is a helper script that runs on that same machine, not a second daemon competing for the same box.
